title: Open restriction of pro-etale direct image with counit normalization
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme], $h:W\hookrightarrow Y$ an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], and $X_W=X\times_YW$, with projections $g:X_W\hookrightarrow X$ and $f_W:X_W\to W$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $R$ be a sheaf of commutative rings on $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], the actual inverse images and direct images [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], coefficient rings $R_X=f^{-1}R$, $R_W=h^{-1}R$ and $R_{X_W}=g^{-1}R_X\cong f_W^{-1}R_W$, and the module adjunctions $f^{-1}\dashv f_*$ and $f_W^{-1}\dashv f_{W,*}$ for these inverse-image coefficient rings [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-adjunction]. For every $R_X$-module sheaf $M$ on $X$, there is a canonical natural isomorphism
$$\beta_M:h^{-1}f_*M\xrightarrow{\sim}f_{W,*}g^{-1}M.$$
Under the open-slice identifications [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-ringed-open-comparison], its evaluation at $E\to W$ is the fibre-product identification $M(X\times_YE)\cong M(X_W\times_WE)$. It is compatible with the specified adjunction counits: writing $\alpha_F:g^{-1}f^{-1}F\xrightarrow{\sim}f_W^{-1}h^{-1}F$ for the canonical inverse-image comparison [lem-weil-pbc-site-morphism-composition], one has
$$g^{-1}(\varepsilon_{f,M})=\varepsilon_{f_W,g^{-1}M}\circ f_W^{-1}(\beta_M)\circ\alpha_{f_*M}.$$
No Noetherian, quasi-compactness, properness, closed-immersion, constant-ring or finiteness assumption is imposed on $f$ or $R$.

source.place: Tag 09A5, section-morphism (base-change evaluation description); with sites.tex Tag 00XZ, section-localize (open slice restriction). The counit equation is a consequence of the inverse-image construction, not a verbatim assertion of these tags.

proof.text: The base-change functors for h:W→Y and g:X_W→X are continuous morphisms of the chosen small pro-etale sites. The base change of the open immersion h is an open immersion, so g is a valid site morphism; the coefficient identifications g^{-1}R_X≅f_W^{-1}R_W are the canonical composition comparison. By the ringed-topos module-adjunction construction, the displayed inverse images and direct images are adjoint with the stated module structures. The composition comparison for inverse images is the unique unit-compatible isomorphism α. Concretely, the two composite base-change functors $u_g\circ u_f$ and $u_{f_W}\circ u_h$ from $Y_{\mathrm{proet}}$ to $(X_W)_{\mathrm{proet}}$ send $V$ to $X_W\times_X(X\times_YV)$ and $X_W\times_W(W\times_YV)$; the fibre-product universal property gives a natural isomorphism $c_V$ between them over $X_W$, compatible with the projections to $X\times_YV$. Define $\alpha$ as the composite of the inverse of the composition isomorphism $(u_g u_f)_s\cong g^{-1}f^{-1}$, the isomorphism $(u_gu_f)_s\cong(u_{f_W}u_h)_s$ induced by $c$, and the composition isomorphism $(u_{f_W}u_h)_s\cong f_W^{-1}h^{-1}$. With the identity coefficient map $f^{-1}R\to R_X$, the module pullback $R_X\otimes_{f^{-1}R}f^{-1}M$ is $f^{-1}M$ and the module counit is the abelian-sheaf counit; likewise for $f_W$ after transport along $\alpha_R$.

source.place: Tag 09A5 (section-morphism), Sites Lemma 03CB and Sites Modules Lemma 03D3

proof.text: Use the open-slice equivalence for the actual inverse-image ringed site. For an object E→W, restriction along h identifies (h^{-1}f_*M)(E) with (f_*M)(E→W→Y), hence with M(X×_Y E) by the direct-image formula. The same equivalence for the base-changed open g identifies (f_{W,*}g^{-1}M)(E) with (g^{-1}M)(X_W×_W E), hence with M(X_W×_W E). The fibre-product universal property gives the canonical isomorphism X_W×_W E≅X×_Y E. These component maps commute with arrows E'→E and are linear for R_W, so they assemble to a natural module-sheaf isomorphism β_M.

proof.text: Counit normalization. Both sides are morphisms of sheaves on $(X_W)_{\mathrm{proet}}$ from $g^{-1}f^{-1}f_*M$ to $g^{-1}M$; module maps with equal underlying abelian maps are equal, so compare underlying maps. Put $N=f_*M$. By the composition isomorphism, the source is $(w_pN)^\#$ for $w=u_g u_f$, and by the universal property of sheafification together with the colimit description of $w_p$, a morphism out of it is determined by its values on the generating sections $[s]_{(V,\psi)}\in(w_pN)(U')$, for $U'\to X_W$, $V\to Y$, $\psi:U'\to X_W\times_X(X\times_YV)$ and $s\in N(V)=M(X\times_YV)$. The adjunction of the continuous-functor pullback lemma is the composite of $u_p\dashv u^p$ and sheafification, so its counit sends the coprojection of $s$ indexed by $(V,\phi)$ to $\phi^*s$, and its unit sends $s$ to the coprojection indexed by $(V,\mathrm{id})$. Hence the map $[s]_{(V,\psi)}\mapsto[[s]_{(V,\mathrm{id})}]_{(X\times_YV,\psi)}$ is compatible with the units; by the uniqueness clause it is the composition isomorphism $(u_gu_f)_s\cong g^{-1}f^{-1}$, and similarly for $u_{f_W}u_h$. Left side: $g^{-1}(\varepsilon_{f,M})$ sends $[[s]_{(V,\mathrm{id})}]_{(X\times_YV,\psi)}$ to $[\varepsilon_f[s]_{(V,\mathrm{id})}]_{(X\times_YV,\psi)}=[s]_{(X\times_YV,\psi)}$. Under $g^{-1}M\cong M|_{X_W}$ (object inverse-image restriction lemma, initial index pair) this is $\bar\psi^*s\in M(U')$, where $\bar\psi:U'\to X\times_YV$ is $\psi$ followed by the projection. Right side: $\alpha$ sends the generator to $[[s]^h_{(V,\mathrm{id})}]_{(E,c_V\psi)}$ with $E=W\times_YV\to W$. Under $h^{-1}N\cong N|_W$, $[s]^h_{(V,\mathrm{id})}$ is $s|_E\in N(E)=M(X\times_YE)$. Then $f_W^{-1}(\beta_M)$ replaces it by $\beta_{M,E}(s|_E)\in(g^{-1}M)(X_W\times_WE)$, which is $s|_E$ transported along $X_W\times_WE\cong X\times_YE$ (step 2). Finally $\varepsilon_{f_W}$ restricts along $c_V\psi:U'\to X_W\times_WE$, giving the restriction of $s$ along $U'\to X_W\times_WE\cong X\times_YE\to X\times_YV$. By the uniqueness in the fibre-product universal property, this composite equals $\bar\psi$: $c_V$ and the identification $X_W\times_WE\cong X\times_YE$ both commute with the projections to $X\times_YV$. The two sides therefore agree on all generating sections, so they are equal. Equivalently, $\beta_M$ is the adjunct (mate) of $g^{-1}(\varepsilon_{f,M})\circ\alpha^{-1}_{f_*M}$ under $f_W^{-1}\dashv f_{W,*}$.
